title: Windows: retired-root fixture paths sit at the Git path-length limit ('$GIT_DIR' too big) and break when the temp root grows by one character
outcome: tests::engram_host_adapter::turn_observations::source_root_naming::retained_runs fixtures (retired_while_named and its labels, e.g. "retired-root-disposition-claim_not_current_for_run") no longer depend on how long the runner's temp root is: their nested project/.worktrees/naming paths stay comfortably under Windows Git's path limit (shorter labels or fixture directory names), so the test outcome cannot change with the checkout or temp location.
acceptance: The retained_runs retired-root fixtures (retired_while_named and its per-case labels, for example retired-root-disposition-claim_not_current_for_run) create project/.worktrees/naming paths whose length no longer depends on the runner's temp-root length in a way that can reach Windows Git's path limit. The fix uses shorter fixture directory names or labels, or a shorter fixed per-test base, and keeps every case's assertions and behavior unchanged. There are no skips, retries, longpaths configuration changes, or test weakening.

The cause is recorded on the item from the original failure: the '$GIT_DIR' too big error, the path length measured at failure, and the margin after the fix for the longest fixture path, computed for the same and a longer temp root. The affected retained_runs tests pass on Windows in a focused run on the exact candidate.
The independent review pair has no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding, and the full gate passes on the exact committed input.

completion.summary: Shortened retired-root fixture labels landed in fdd8d035; assertions unchanged, exact-candidate Windows focused 27 PASS, independent pairs zero Medium+, Windows B and Linux FULLs PASS on identical landed tree.
